Done. You have a working browser-based 2D CAD editor in `D:\physics\cad` — open `index.html` in any browser, no build step or dependencies. I verified it headlessly: drew all entity types via simulated mouse/keyboard with zero console errors, confirmed the rendering visually via screenshot, and validated that the SVG and DXF exporters produce well-formed output.

**What's in it:**

- **Drawing tools** — line (auto-chains like AutoCAD), polyline (Enter/double-click to finish, `C` to close), rectangle, circle, 3-point arc, linear dimensions (with extension lines, arrows, and live measurement text), and text. Shift gives ortho lock while drawing.
- **Snapping** — adaptive grid snap (1-2-5 spacing that follows zoom) plus object snap to endpoints, midpoints, centers, and circle quadrants, each with its own marker shape (square/triangle/circle). Toggle with `G`/`O` or the status-bar buttons.
- **Selection & editing** — click or Shift+click; drag right for window select, drag left for crossing select (AutoCAD-style). Drag a selection to move, Ctrl+drag to copy, Delete to remove, 100-level undo/redo.
- **Layers** — per-layer color and visibility, entities colored by-layer with per-entity override in the properties panel.
- **View** — wheel zoom at cursor, pan with middle/right drag or Space+drag, `F` to fit. World coordinates are y-up (CAD convention) with red X / green Y axes.
- **Files** — save/open JSON, export SVG, and export DXF R12 (opens in AutoCAD, LibreCAD, QCAD). The drawing also auto-saves to localStorage so refreshing doesn't lose work.

Press `?` in the app for the full shortcut list; `README.md` documents everything. The code is split as `index.html` (layout), `style.css` (dark theme), and `app.js` (~1,100 lines: entity model, snapping, tools, rendering, exporters) — so it's straightforward to extend with things like trim/fillet, more dimension types, or DXF import if you want to go further.
